extracted.intended_audience: readers, students, and critics of 19th-century literature interested in George Sand
extracted.subtask_description: A close critical-essay style survey that collects and recalls the governing motives, principal elements, and evolution of George Sand's work and person, intended to help readers understand her literary strain and social ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment of the ideal life (ruling motive)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Le sentiment de la vie idéale, qui n'est autre que la vie normale telle que nous sommes appelés à la connaître" — the sentiment of the ideal life is the ruling thought of George Sand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'sentiment of the ideal life' is the ground-motive that animates her whole work; the critic should view her oeuvre through this lens to understand recurring aims and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cry of agony and revolt
rubrics_metrics.description: One principal element of her strain is the passion of agony and revolt, prominent in her earlier work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early works (e.g., Lélia, Valentine, Werther-like pieces) manifest grandiose, moving cadences and intense rebellion; this element fades in later writings but is essential to understanding her youthful force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolation from nature and beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: A central element is trust in nature and beauty as a consoling and restorative force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Her second movement emphasizes intimate, faithful depictions of rural nature (wild-flowers by actual names, lanes, meadows, oxen, etc.), which introduce suavity into her grief and passion and form a major source of her moral and aesthetic authority (e.g., Valentine, La Mare au Diable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspiration toward social renewal (renaissance sociale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas of social renewal and a belief in equality and fraternity form a third principal element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Her fiction and polemic consistently advocate social equality as the future and foundational ideal; the social-moral aim should be foregrounded when assessing her work and ideology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolution of the three elements across her career
rubrics_metrics.description: The three elements (revolt, nature/beauty, social renewal) evolve over forty years: the cry of revolt appears early and passes away; trust in nature and social ideals gain prominence later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should consider chronological development: do not judge Sand by one period alone; understanding shifts in emphasis is key to a fair assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity and unfailing resolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Her pursuit of the ruling motive is characterized by most unfailing resolve and absolute sincerity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate her works with attention to moral earnestness and consistency of purpose rather than only technical or genre standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not reducible to charming stories or character-creation alone
rubrics_metrics.description: George Sand is more than a maker of charming stories or a creator of attractive characters; her full spirit goes through her work as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reducing her to a subset (e.g., judging her solely by Consuelo); assess the larger thematic and moral currents that run through multiple works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative works for comprehending her strain
rubrics_metrics.description: A small, well-chosen selection (e.g., Lettres d'un Voyageur, Mauprat, François le Champi, Valvèdre) can suffice to show her principal elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three or four representative texts may be enough for readers to apprehend her central themes and evolution; critics should prefer representative sampling to selective elevation of single works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and cordial simplicity of manner/persona
rubrics_metrics.description: Her personal manner and the personae she creates often make an impression of frank, cordial simplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This simplicity (in manners, tone, outlook) is a defining trait and should be noted when characterizing her authorial voice and public persona.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intimate, faithful depiction of rural life and concrete detail
rubrics_metrics.description: She keeps readers closely and truly intimate with rural nature and peasant life, using concrete details (names of wild-flowers, lanes, oxen, farmhouse scenes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should account for the ethnographic fidelity and sensual specificity of her rural descriptions, which supply both charm and moral purpose to her fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peasant as central figure and emblem of France/future
rubrics_metrics.description: The peasant is the central figure in her rural world and stands for France, life, and the future; she sees the peasant as the minister in a vast temple and as bearer of equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretations should foreground how she elevates peasant life ethically and politically, and how this shapes her social optimism and prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joy and harmony between mind, heart, and hands
rubrics_metrics.description: Joy (the feeling that life is good) and a harmony of mind, heart, and hands are essential to her ideal of a fruitful life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical readings should note her emphasis that labour integrated with understanding and feeling leads to human flourishing; the ideal of the laborer-as-artist recurs as a moral image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious stance: rejection of dogma, affirmation of a 'divine sense'
rubrics_metrics.description: She rejects idolatrous dogma but affirms a vague 'divine sense' or presence in nature and humanity, equating true religion with inward conscience and universal divinity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating her moral philosophy, account for this mystical-humanist religiosity rather than orthodox beliefs; it links her aesthetic and social thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social equality and liberal-social ideals as moral-religious creed
rubrics_metrics.description: Equality (social liberty and fraternal equality) is held as an ideal, philosophy, and religion—the goal of man and the law of the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should treat her political pronouncements as integral to her literary vision; her passionate advocacy for equality explains many thematic choices and may explain rhetorical intensity in polemic passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and memorable cadences (language resists translation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Her early work contains grandiose, moving sentences with persistent cadences that haunt the memory; her language sometimes defies translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should pay attention to sentence-music, rhythmic effects, and linguistic particularities when judging her prose; translations may lose essential tonal qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defence of the people (peasantry) against elite contempt
rubrics_metrics.description: A recurring stance is defence of the peasant and critique of contempt from educated elites; she values probity, charity, tact, and simple humane virtues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read her social criticism as an ethical corrective aimed at elites; evaluations should note how literary representation and political sympathy reinforce one another.
